subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core provider-family fallback contract for model refs, and if so should it be wildcard/auto refs, grouped fallbackFamilies, or a narrower catalog-derived fallback?
rationale: This would define public config and provider-routing behavior in a compatibility-sensitive fallback path, and AGENTS.md treats fallback behavior as a product decision rather than an implementation convenience.

options.title: Define one core fallback contract
options.body: Choose one public contract and implement it across schema, docs, candidate resolution, availability gates, and upgrade/doctor behavior.

options.title: Limit scope to catalog-derived fallbacks
options.body: Use the narrower https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/60922 direction if maintainers want explicit opt-in catalog reuse but not wildcard or grouped family semantics.

options.title: Decline new core config for now
options.body: Keep explicit fallbacks as the supported path and direct dynamic provider policy to plugin hooks or external tooling until stronger product demand appears.

recommendation.title: Define one core fallback contract
recommendation.body: Choose one public contract and implement it across schema, docs, candidate resolution, availability gates, and upgrade/doctor behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current fallback/config history signal and appears in blame on the inspected schema and resolver lines.
